item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
1-" SCP-956-1's effects vary depending upon the age of the human consuming them. Humans at the age of 12 years or older go into a seizure within █ minutes of consumption, with a █% possibility of cardiac arrest. There is an approximate ██% chance of survival for such subjects. "

+ show block
– hide block

This is very silly, for a 1 digit % chance to even happen (1%-9%) you need to have done this at least 11 times (1/11=9%) but then you show a 2 digit chance of survival so that means that there are at least 2 children that had cardiac arrest meaning you have done this experiment at least 21 times. (2/21=9.5%) (Putting the lives of at least 20 children at risk + the one that died for the experiment to be possible in the first place and actually killing at least 2 (The one who had a heart attack and the one who died so the experiment could be possible)).

2-" Their body then [DATA REDACTED]. "

Lazy writing, but this comes down to a disdain I have in general when it comes to redacting/blackboxing info in articles, if the article is written with SCP employees in mind as readers then you surely would want to give them as much info as possible that doesn't risk the security of anyone.

3- "18 by 18 by 4 meter"

You don't need 1296³m of area to accommodate a single small pinata. If you're specifying that then what's to say you shouldn't specify the position of the door within the cell? The height of the cell when compared to the sea? Just get around all that and say it should be stored in a: "Standard humanoid cell" and decrease the clutter on the reader's eyes.

4- The writer puts goddamn O5s and Level 4s on the article as well as a guard looking over it at all times (Assigning a guard full time to watch over 1 single SCP that never attempted breach 24/7 is not going to come cheap). As if this thing was so incredibly dangerous, it isn't. No need for all this set up.

5- The setup they make about striking out "Safe" and putting in "Euclid" (it wandering around and looking in the direction of an elementary school) did payoff in my opinion. It wasn't bombastic but it was believable and let us wanting more (which I like personally).

In closing, it is a decent SCP and apart from the bad usage of Redaction all other bad things were passable. I enjoyed the end particularly, just pretend that it doesn't read "O5" and instead "Site Director" which would be much more believable. Solid 5/10 (I realize that makes me sound very egocentric but hey.) I'm not sure about whether it should be a +1 or not so for now I'll opt for the +1.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.content:encoded:
If you can reach the author, they can either make the changes or give authorization for them. Aside from that, we need either a plummet in the upvotes, getting this to deletion range, or a very special situation where such a change is deemed a huge improvement to the community besides all the potential downsides, and there are many of those.

You can try for a side avenue by writing yourself a "corrected" version elsewhere and then showing it around. If it is good enough, you can actually improve your chances of getting an author approval or convincing people to downvote the current version, but outside of author approval I think it quite unlikely that this will change anytime whatsoever.

item.content:encoded:
The point isn't so much that the D-Class is someone that deserved to die, as you seem to think. Deciding who deserves it or not is a huge box of ethical problems even with just USA's Death Row inmates.

At the end of the day, a Death Row inmate of any nation is someone who WILL be executed, regardless of whatever put them there. Their lives was already forfeit, and by reaching them the Foundation just re-purposes those executions without actual judgement.

Keep in mind that the Foundation focus on remaining neutral to politics. They won't start to say who should have Death Penalty and who shouldn't regardless of the D-Class program, they have no saying on whom gets the penalty. The only thing they have is a need for people that can be killed or put in extreme danger, and the choices that come with it.

item.title: Slight edit idea
item.content:encoded:
Slight edit idea: It says that children under the age of 12 who consume SCP-956-1 transform into another SCP-956 after █ minutes, but it doesn't say the new ones are terminated, nor does it say anywhere that the SCP-956 can be destroyed.

What I would want to know is how many of these things exist in the fictional SCP world. They probably did the test more than once to see if turning into SCP-956 was the only consequence if a child under 12 ate SCP-956-1, and again, it doesn't say they were terminated.

item.content:encoded:
Wow. Is that the creepiest pinata ever, or what? The part about it knowing exactly where the elementary school was… and that it was looking at it the entire time…. *shudder*.

Only one nitpick. SCP-956-1 is never defined. It's easy to tell from the context that SCP-956-1 is the candy that spills out of a victim's torso when cracked open, with references to it being "consumed", but you never actually come out and say it's the candy. I feel like that's an oversite in a scientific document. I would suggest changing the following:

"Upon breach, the victim's body discharges large pile of unmarked candy, ranging from ██ to ████ pieces."

To:

"Upon breach, the victim's body discharges large pile of unmarked candy, ranging from ██ to ████ pieces. Instances of this candy are referred to as SCP-956-1."
